prose:ch04-objectives:
Chapter objectives. This chapter will help readers to:

  • Define a health workforce registry and related terms in plain language.
  • Explain what “authoritative source” means and how it can be achieved with one system or several.
  • Show how the registry supports each stage of the health worker life cycle and its main strategic uses.
prose:ch04-key-messages:
Key messages

  • The registry holds a minimum set of trusted information that uniquely identifies each health worker, their qualifications, their authorization to practise and where they work.
  • “Authoritative” refers to the information and the rules for maintaining it, not to a single database.
  • Each data item should have one accountable owner. The registry brings these items together.
  • The registry is not an HRIS, but HRIS, regulatory and payroll systems should all supply data to it and draw on it.
prose:ch04-definitions:
• Working definitions of health workforce registry, professional register, HRIS, health worker, registration, licence and credential (see Glossary annex).
  • Alignment with the WHO 2015 minimum data set definition (“the single authoritative source of health workforce information”) and with the draft DPI-H reference architecture.
  • The difference between a “registry” (the shared national capability) and a “register” (a regulator's legal list of those authorized to practise).
prose:ch04-authoritative-source:
• Which institution is the source of truth for each data item, such as identity, qualification, licence status and employment.
  • How records from several sources are matched to one unique health worker identifier.
  • Options: a single national system, or several source systems connected to give one consistent view.
prose:ch04-health-worker-lifecycle:
• Stages: pre-service education, graduation, registration and licensing, employment and deployment, continuing professional development, renewal, mobility, exit and re-entry.
  • The events at each stage that create or change registry data, and who records them.
  • Link to the NHWA health labour market framework (education, labour force, and serving population health needs).

prose:ch04-strategic-uses:
• Regulation and public protection: confirming that practitioners are qualified and in good standing.
  • Planning and management: stock, distribution, skill mix, attrition and migration.
  • Service delivery and digital health: identifying and authorizing health workers in electronic records, prescribing, telehealth and payment systems.

Expected outputs for countries

  • An agreed national definition and purpose statement for the registry.
  • A map of the authoritative source for each data item.
prose:ch05-objectives:
Chapter objectives. This chapter will help readers to:

  • Identify the people and systems that supply or use registry information.
  • Prioritize a small set of use cases to drive the first phase.
  • Show how personas, use cases and user stories are turned into requirements.
prose:ch05-key-messages:
Key messages

  • Requirements should come from real users and tasks, not from software features.
  • Systems are users too: many registry “users” are other applications requesting information through interfaces.
  • Start with a few high-value use cases and add more over time.
  • The generic personas and use cases are a starting point. Countries need to adapt them.
prose:ch05-personas:
• People: health worker, registration officer in a regulatory body, employer or facility human resources manager, training institution registrar, workforce planner, member of the public, emergency coordinator.
  • Systems: HRIS, payroll, electronic medical record, facility registry, national identity system, NHWA platform.
  • For each persona: goals, tasks, difficulties, digital skills and connectivity.
pers:health-worker:
Persona. Health worker

Person. A person whose job is to protect and improve the health of their community: holds a registration, licence and employment record in the registry, and needs portable, verifiable credentials and simple renewals.

Specialises the SMART Guidelines generic persona: HealthcareProvider; CommunityHealthWorker.

Draft for working-group review Outline basis
Goals Portable, verifiable credentials; simpler renewals; recognition of training and continuing professional development; able to see and correct their own record. 1.4, 6.3, 12.3
Tasks Apply for registration and licence; renew with CPD recorded; update employment or place of practice; view and correct own record; present a digital credential for verification online or offline. 5.2, 7.3, 12.3, 20.1, 20.2
Difficulties Slow licensing; duplicate records across systems; administrative burden of re-entering the same data; concerns about how their data are used. 1.1, 15 (key messages), 14.4, 18.1
Digital skills Varies. Paper or assisted channels are kept where digital skills are limited. To confirm with country input. 15.2
Connectivity Varies, including low-connectivity settings; credentials must be verifiable offline. To confirm with country input. 7 (key messages), 8.3, 20.2
pers:registration-officer:
Persona. Registration officer (regulatory body)

Person. Staff of a professional council or regulatory body who registers and licenses practitioners, records status changes and answers verification requests.

Draft for working-group review Outline basis
Goals An accurate register that protects the public by confirming who is qualified and in good standing; faster, cheaper registration, renewal and verification. 1.2, 4.4
Tasks Register and license practitioners; verify qualifications with training institutions; record status changes (suspended, lapsed, reinstated); answer verification requests, including from other countries; issue certificates of good standing. 7.3, 7.4, 20.1, 20.4
Difficulties Records on paper or in stand-alone systems; duplicate records; concern about loss of control over their data and workload. 1.1, 13.2, 14.4
Digital skills To confirm with country input. —
Connectivity To confirm with country input. —
pers:employer-hr-manager:
Persona. Employer or facility human resources manager

Person. Recruits, deploys and manages health workers for a public or private employer or facility; verifies credentials and records changes of employment and place of practice.

Specialises the SMART Guidelines generic persona: HealthSystemManager.

Draft for working-group review Outline basis
Goals Confidence that staff are qualified and authorized to practise; payroll that matches the real workforce. 1.2, 1.4
Tasks Verify a health worker's status before and during employment; record changes of employment and place of practice; act on notices of suspension. 5.2, 7.3, 20.1, 20.2
Difficulties Unverified credentials; duplicate and ghost records; data re-entered across HR and payroll systems. 1.1, 9 (key messages)
Digital skills To confirm with country input. —
Connectivity To confirm with country input. —

Persona. Training institution registrar

Person. Records enrolment and graduation in a pre-service education institution and confirms qualifications to the regulator.

Draft for working-group review Outline basis

Person. Uses stock, distribution, skill mix, attrition and migration data for planning and NHWA reporting.

prose:ch05-priority-use-cases:
• Register and license a new graduate; renew a licence; update employment or place of practice.
  • Verify a health worker's status (by an employer, a patient, another system or another country).
  • Produce workforce counts and distribution for planning and NHWA reporting.
scen:register-and-license-new-graduate:
User-scenario. Register and license a new graduate

A new graduate applies for registration; the qualification is verified with the training institution; the regulator registers and licenses the graduate; the registry record is created with a unique health worker identifier.

Personas: Health worker, Training institution registrar, Registration officer (regulatory body)
